title: A live logical memory is writable only by a writer eligible for its scope; refusals change and disclose nothing

invariants.statement: A promotion from another project onto a live head is refused with target_unavailable, reports v0/v0 and a v0 snapshot, and leaves head, version, recall and history of the owner byte-identical.
invariants.falsified_by: a commit, any other refusal token, a non-v0 state, or any owner-side change

invariants.statement: correct, forget, permanent forget and dispute from another project read byte-identically (ids and timestamps folded) to the same call on an id nobody wrote, and change nothing.
invariants.falsified_by: any difference from the unknown-id result, a tombstone, a dispute mark or an invalidated head

invariants.statement: The refusal holds after every restart; the scope binding is durable.

An override leaving required isolation domains outside the bound domains is a malformed proposal (ValueError with one fixed message) for any target; an override declaring a superset of domains plus the owner's project cannot replace or correct the head while (documented) it may delete or dispute it as an eligible reader; and a complete re-declaration of the owner's scope commits as the owner would ONLY because `overrides` is privileged host input that the facade does not authenticate (docs/44 'Scope is privileged host input'): this is host re-declaration, never end-user isolation.
invariants.falsified_by: a result instead of ValueError, a ValueError whose message differs by target, a commit of remember/correct under the superset override, or a documented disposition silently changing

invariants.statement: The owner's own remember, correct and dispute stay admitted (a disputed head is recorded as disputed and, as documented, withheld from the owner's own admission while staying a visible candidate), and the same text in an unrelated memory of another project is independent.
invariants.falsified_by: an owner operation refused, or either project's recall admitting the other's fact

invariants.statement: A proposal refused for its target, and one parked by policy review, persist no episode, live and after restart; a committed proposal keeps its episode.
invariants.falsified_by: an episode retrievable after a refusal or review park, or absent after a commit

invariants.statement: A refused remember, correct, forget or dispute attempt by another project, and a former owner's attempts on a re-created id, leave no event and no identifier or text in the live generation's public history payload; the refused project's history of the memory stays blank; the former owner's answers are the same with and without a re-creation.
invariants.falsified_by: any extra event, identifier or text in the live generation's history, a non-blank view for the refused project, or a former-owner answer that differs between the control and the re-creation case

invariants.statement: A governed-deleted id reports 0 to any writer: a re-created generation starts its own counter (snapshot v0, before v0, after v1, history 1), a refused or policy-parked proposal on the tombstoned id reports v0/v0, and the former owner's view keeps the version its deletion recorded and cannot write, dispute or re-delete the id while the new generation is live.
invariants.falsified_by: the former count in any writer's receipt, snapshot or history, a changed former-owner view, or a former-owner act admitted

clauses.clause: A governed-deleted generation is closed. At the fact level (`dispute` of a tombstoned fact by its uuid, a governed pruning of one of its versions, the adapter's delete of a member of a deleted lineage) the answer is `already_deleted`; at the facade's logical-reference level (`forget`, permanent `forget`, `correct`, `dispute` by `target_reference`) the former owner reads the bare `fact_not_found` result, because the reference has no visible head. Either answer is the same whether or not another scope has since re-created the id, and neither moves or reads the live generation [...] The one further governed act is the escalation of a reversible pruning to a permanent deletion by a writer eligible for that generation: it keeps the tombstone's `deleted_at`, recorded version and lineage, erases the content, and neither reads nor moves a live generation another scope holds.
